messages:
sarah: Heads up — after the Karpenter migration in us-west-2 we saw a spike in failed GPU pod launches, looks like ENI allocation errors during warmup.

miguel: same here in prod-ml yesterday, lots of Pending pods with `FailedScheduling: node/ENIQuotaExceeded`. Pods never hit Ready.

sarah: kube events excerpt: `Warning FailedScheduling ... failed to find nodes that match resource requests -> node/ENIQuotaExceeded` and later `FailedAttachVolume` spam.

kai: @eng-sre can we get per-AZ ENI allocations vs warmpool counts? suspect warmpool + consolidation race. :thinking_face: 

ops-bot: ALERT gpu-pool-1 ENI exhaustion (us-west-2a) — 5m spike, 37 failed attachments.

miguel: quick theory: Karpenter creates short-lived nodes to warm GPU cache, then consolidation tries to remove them before ENI detach finishes, causing extra ENI churn. Also we might be hitting instance ENI soft limits.

anne: provisioning YAML for the provisioner: `consolidation: {enabled: true}` and warmpool configured with `min:1` per-az. We didn't anticipate concurrent warm requests across many jobs.

sean: check NIC trunking and ENI-per-instance limits for the GPU instance families we use (p4d/p3). Some AZs have lower account-level ENI quotas too. Might be quota exhaustion upstream.

miguel: reproduction steps i used locally:
```
kubectl run gpu-bench --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorflow:latest-gpu --requests='cpu=4,memory=30Gi,nvidia.com/gpu=1' --replicas=12
# watch events: kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod
```
This pushes many simultaneous node provisions in the same AZ.

matt: short-term mitigation proposal: bump warmpool min from 1 -> 3 in the two busiest AZs and temporarily set `consolidation.enabled: false` for the GPU provisioner so we avoid scale-in churn while we debug.

anne: cost tradeoff: increasing warmpool to 3 across 2 AZs ~ estimated +$220/day in on-demand GPU spend (ballpark). Need finance signoff for > 48h.

sarah: operational playbook note: if ENI errors persist, fallback to a dedicated nodepool (managed ASG) for production-critical workloads so we bypass ENI churn from rapid provision/terminate cycles.

kai: i'll run an audit: list all instance types used by gpu provisioners and query ENI limits + account quotas, then map to traffic patterns by AZ. Will share a spreadsheet.

miguel: also consider adding a readiness gate: delay marking the node Ready to scheduler until NVidia driver + kubelet fully initialized, reduces pod reschedules during attach. We can implement a `startupProbe` or init container that blocks readiness until `nvidia-smi` shows GPU present.

sean: another angle: tune `maxNodeProvisionTime` lower so Karpenter gives up faster and avoids partial attach states? not sure. Need to test.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for `provisioner/warmpool-size` change in us-west-2 (2 AZs). Monitor: gpu-pool-1, gpu-pool-2.

matt: actionable recap: 1) bump warmpool to 3 in hot AZs (canary) 2) audit ENI limits per instance type & account quota 3) add node readiness gating for GPU nodes 4) test consolidation toggle impact in staging 5) cost estimate and finance approval.

anne: i'll prepare the cost memo and open a short-lived change window for the canary.

sarah: thanks all — if we see >10% failed attachments in the next hour, revert canary and route critical traffic to dedicated pool. :thumbsup:
